# Your Toolkit

This part asks what you work with every day and how you keep a
history of that work. It belongs to the first quarter, and every
later chapter assumes it: the commands, the editor, and the version
history introduced here are used without further explanation from
Part III onward.

- @sec-shell teaches the Unix shell: moving around the filesystem,
  inspecting a raw file before R reads it, and composing pipelines.
- @sec-workstation installs R, an IDE, Quarto, and Git, and verifies
  the machine with a checklist.
- @sec-git-solo introduces Git and GitHub for a single analyst who
  wants a recoverable history.
- @sec-git-teams extends that history to a team: branches, pull
  requests, review, and conflicts.
- @sec-ai-coding sets out how to prompt language models and coding
  agents, how to check what they produce, and what may be sent to
  them, before you rely on them in the chapters that follow.

If the quiz at the start of a chapter is easy, skip to the next. A
reader who already uses Git daily may move quickly through
@sec-git-solo, but should still read @sec-ai-governance before
sending any project file to a model.
